FAKE-SYNTHETIC demo visit note: synthetic data, roles only.
Visit notes, Sunrise Care Partners 025 (Florida IDN; primary care is the main facility type). Met the pharmacy director and the immunization lead in the main clinic conference room.

The book is about $835K in net dollars, a solid slice of the in-state total among the synthetic peers and a small slice of national dollars. I walked the pharmacy director through that size snapshot first so we were looking at the same scale.

We spent most of the visit on pneumococcal, which leads the mix at roughly half of dollars, well ahead of the national share, with a high index versus both the national file and in-state peers. The immunization lead already tracks that dollar share. I asked what is driving purchasing in pneumococcal and which programs are planned for next season. They pointed to standing orders in the primary care clinics and a planned fall clinic calendar, and asked for a one-page leave-behind on those programs.

On hepatitis, the share for Merck & Company moved down sharply between the two windows (from the high seventies to under half of class doses). The pharmacy director had seen that share move and asked for a follow-up view of the two windows.

Must-cover items we walked in full: HPV to MenACWY plus MenABCWY doses is low for this system against the pooled national file, and they agreed the adolescent platform needs a closer look before the next school cycle. Dollar share of shingles is well above in-state peers; they want to hold that volume and asked for a short peer comparison. We also confirmed the pneumococcal dollar share versus in-state peers, which is the other must-cover on the mix.

The MSA is live into early 2027 and does not renew automatically. No further meeting was set; I will send the two leave-behinds this week.
